Based on the provided source, here is the extracted information:

### Bibliographic Metadata
*   **Title:** Data-Driven Parameter Identification of Synchronous Generators: A Three-Stage Framework with State Consistency and Grid Decoupling (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075048)
*   **Authors:** Rasool Peykarporsan, Tharuka Govinda Waduge, Tek Tjing Lie, Martin Stommel (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075048)
*   **Journal:** *Sensors* (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075048)
*   **Publication Date:** 2026 (Volume 26, Issue 7, Article 2024) (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075048)
*   **DOI:** 10.3390/s26072024 (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075048)

### Study Design
*   The study proposes and validates a comprehensive three-stage data-driven identification framework for Port-Hamiltonian (PH) modeling of synchronous generators. (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075048)
*   The framework utilizes sensor-acquired voltage and current signals to capture system dynamics while remaining compatible with PH model structures. (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075048)

### Population
*   The "population" in this engineering context refers to synchronous generators, which are identified as the central dynamic component of modern power systems. (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075048)

### Interventions
The proposed three-stage framework incorporates the following methodological interventions to overcome existing gaps:
*   **Multi-scenario excitation:** Utilizing sensor-acquired voltage and current signals across multiple scenarios. (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075048)
*   **Derivative-free state consistency optimization:** Addressing noise sensitivity issues found in traditional derivative-based formulations. (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075048)
*   **Physics-based regularization:** Enforcing PH structure preservation to ensure physically meaningful and reliable stability indices. (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075048)

### Outcomes
*   **Parameter Identification:** Complete identification of eight key synchronous generator parameters: $H, D, X_d, X_q, X'_d, X'_q, T'_{do}, T'_{qo}$. (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075048)
*   **Accuracy:** Parameter identification errors ranged from 1.26% to 9.10%. (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075048)
*   **Validation Metrics:** Validation confirmed RMS rotor angle errors below 1.2° and speed errors below 0.15%. (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075048)

### Findings
*   The proposed framework successfully resolves fundamental limitations associated with IEEE Standard 115, which include single-scenario identifiability constraints, noise-sensitive derivative-based formulations that amplify sensor measurement errors, and the inability to decouple generator-internal damping from grid contributions. (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075048)
*   The framework addresses five fundamental limitations in existing methods, enabling complete eight-parameter identification with high fidelity. (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075048)
*   The results demonstrate the framework's suitability for transient stability analysis, passivity-based control design, and oscillation damping assessment. (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075048)

### Limitations
*   **Online Tracking:** The current Stage 3 pipeline is not yet a continuous sliding-window estimator; future work is required to adapt it for online parameter tracking. (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075048)
*   **Contextual Limitations:** The text explicitly details the limitations of the *existing* methods (IEEE Standard 115) that the study aimed to fix—namely single-scenario identifiability, noise amplification, and grid decoupling issues—rather than highlighting failures of the newly proposed framework itself. (Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075048)
